incident-bot: PAGED: private-connectivity-alert for customer ToneLab — Private VPC peering route suppression detected in eu-west1-az3. Severity: P1. @maria-oncall is on call.

maria-oncall: I'm on it. seeing spike in 5xxs from ToneLab's ingress in eu-west1. dashboards show 100% of their traffic hitting failures from az3.

kevin-netops: preliminary BGP metrics show path withdraws from our peering session to AZ3 at ~1934567870. Might be a route flap/propagation issue on provider side.

sophie-sre: can you paste the BGP neighbor state and last updates? also any DNS overrides? ToneLab is using a PrivateLink endpoint so DNS for the endpoint is crucial.

kevin-netops: attaching quick copy of relevant outputs:

```
# show bgp summary neighbor 10.200.8.1
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcvd MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.200.8.1      4 65222   12345   12340        0    0    0 00:12:13        0

# show bgp routes | match 10.250.0.0/24
* 10.250.0.0/24  0.0.0.0 via 10.200.9.254, indirect, suppressed
```

kevin-netops: note the Prefix is being marked suppressed in AZ3's RIB. my hypothesis: upstream provider (cloud fabric) has a control-plane instability for that AZ causing route to be temporarily de-preferred and then not re-advertised to peering.

maria-oncall: DNS check: dig against the private zone for ToneLab endpoint returns the expected PrivateLink A record on AZ1 and AZ2, but queries from AZ3 are returning NXDOMAIN or stale cached entries.

lia-cs: lia-cs here, I've informed the ToneLab SE (ryan-se) that we're investigating and requested they avoid configuration changes. Customer impact: their admin UI reports service 503 for ~12 minutes, mass retries.

ryan-se: ok thanks. customer will pause heavy jobs. any ETA for mitigation?

sophie-sre: short-term mitigation options: 1) withdraw AZ3 peering from routing (force traffic away) 2) request cloud provider to accelerate route propagation/fix control plane 3) create temporary PrivateConnect path from AZ1/2 to ToneLab's transit (requires config + TAC). I recommend option 1 as fastest if it won't cause bigger outage.

kevin-netops: I can set a local policy to lower preference/weight for routes coming from AZ3 so peers prefer AZ1/2. Doing a conservative prep first.

maria-oncall: go ahead Kevin, do it with a canary: change on one edge router, monitor, then roll. Keep TTL short.

kevin-netops: executing: `conf t 
route-map DEPRIORITIZE-AZ3 permit 10
 set local-preference 50` then applied to BGP neighbor for az3.

```
# output
*Route-map applied to neighbor 10.200.8.1
BGP: outbound update sent
```

kevin-netops: change applied on edge-01. Monitoring route table and customer traffic.

maria-oncall: verifying customer healthchecks... metrics show 60% drop in errors within 30s of the change. ToneLab UI reports partial recovery. :thumbsup:

lia-cs: passing interim update to ToneLab: "We have implemented a traffic steering change to route around the affected AZ. Engineers are working with the cloud provider for a durable fix."

sophie-sre: good. open a provider ticket with the control-plane trace and ask for route-table reconciliation for eu-west1-az3. include BGP OPEN/UPDATE dumps.

kevin-netops: ticket opened: CLOUD-89421. provider response initial: "investigating fabric control plane, will push fix to normalize route advertisement." ETA unknown.

maria-oncall: action items: 1) keep traffic steer in place until provider confirms stable 2) gather packet captures/traceroute from az3 -> private endpoint 3) coordinate final rollback once verified. I'll stay on call with netops.

ryan-se: customer update sent: "We routed traffic away from the impacted AZ, service is recovering, engineering is coordinating with the provider. We'll confirm full restoration and follow up."

kevin-netops: traceroute from AZ3 to endpoint now shows indirect route via AZ1 after steering: 

```
traceroute to pl-01.tonelab.internal (10.250.1.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.200.9.1 (10.200.9.1)  1.12 ms  1.08 ms  0.98 ms
 2  10.200.1.11 (10.200.1.11)  2.15 ms  2.09 ms  2.03 ms
 3  10.250.1.12 (10.250.1.12)  3.22 ms  3.17 ms  3.11 ms
```

maria-oncall: logs confirm reduced 5xxs and no new NXDOMAINs from AZ3 resolvers.

sophie-sre: once provider confirms, we should reverse the route-map and let normal advertisement resume. Also add automated detection rule: if peering prefix is suppressed > 30s, alert netops and trigger auto-steer.

kevin-netops: agreed. file follow-up: add runbook step and PagerDuty monitor (BGP_PREFIX_SUPPRESSED) to trigger automatic weigh-change.

maria-oncall: closing notes for postmortem: root cause suspected provider control-plane instability in eu-west1 AZ3 causing route suppression for peered prefix -> impacted PrivateLink DNS resolution and subsequent 503s for ToneLab. Immediate mitigation: local preference steering away from AZ3 normalized customer traffic. Customer-facing: temporary degraded but restored within ~4 minutes after steering. Follow-up: provider fix confirmation + runbook automation + postmortem.

deploy-bot: incident log recorded: ID INC-2026-1934567890.

lia-cs: I'll send final update to ToneLab once provider confirms.

maria-oncall: handing off to postmortem owner kevin-netops for full RCA and to sophie-sre for automation work. staying available for questions. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated).
